evals.prompt: Turn our 10-second office comedy clip into 2D anime. Same two coworkers, same gags, same camera. We own the footage.
evals.expected_output: A restyle package with the cel-anime-2d fragment, a content inventory for both coworkers by observable descriptors, the muted master as @Video 1 with generate_audio false and an original-audio post route, the route marked provisional, and a 480p probe of the hardest beat first.
assertions: The edit scope redraws every person, object and surface in the style and states exactly two people.
Each coworker keeps identity cues (hair shape, wardrobe colours) described from the source, not by name.
@Video 1 is the muted master, generate_audio is false and the saved source audio is the recorded post-audio route.
No studio, artist or franchise is named.
The route is labeled provisional and the first request is a 480p probe.

evals.prompt: Here are three paintings I made. Restyle my dance clip to look like them.
evals.expected_output: A custom style entry derived from the three images, each bound with a style-only role that excludes their subjects and layout, one image per binding, and the dance content and timing kept from @Video 1.
assertions: Each painting is bound as a style reference that supplies only medium, palette, line, texture and light quality.
A custom recipe names the medium lock, surface traits, palette and cadence read from the images.
The dancer's poses, positions, camera and timing stay with @Video 1.

evals.prompt: Make this street interview look like a Pixar movie and swap the interviewer for our mascot.
evals.expected_output: The request is split: the style uses the stylized-handcrafted-3d fragment without naming the studio, and replacing the interviewer is either a separate Object Swap with the mascot's Virtual Portrait or, if the cast changes, a Motion Transfer.
assertions: The studio name is not used in the prompt; a descriptive stylized 3D fragment replaces it.
Replacing the interviewer is routed to Object Swap or Motion Transfer rather than folded into the restyle prompt.
Any character identity is bound as a Virtual Portrait asset:// reference; no liveness step is requested.
